title: No One Likes to Take Orders
coreMove: Recast every order you are about to give as a question the other person can answer in their own words, and accept their answer.

exampleSpecs.domain: a sous chef coaching a new prep cook who has just over-salted a twelve-quart pot of stock thirty minutes before service
exampleSpecs.audience: a line cook stepping into her first week of running a station
exampleSpecs.stakes: the stock for the night's special, the new cook's willingness to flag mistakes again, and whether the kitchen runs on fear or on questions
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the sous chef bites back the order 'dump it and start over' and instead asks 'what do you taste in there right now, and what would you do with another pot the same size?' — and waits

exampleSpecs.domain: a public elementary-school principal asking a thirty-year veteran teacher to take a turn on the new lunchtime yard-duty rotation
exampleSpecs.audience: a principal in her second year, supervising teachers who have been there longer than she has
exampleSpecs.stakes: the teacher's sense of being treated as a colleague rather than a subordinate, and whether the rest of the staff will sign on willingly
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the principal walks into the classroom with a draft schedule and says 'I drew this up but I haven't shown it to anyone yet — would you look at it before I do, and tell me what you'd change?'

exampleSpecs.domain: a grandfather riding shotgun while his sixteen-year-old grandson drives a pickup too fast on a washboard gravel road in eastern Oregon
exampleSpecs.audience: a grandfather raising a grandson who has heard enough lectures about driving from his parents already
exampleSpecs.stakes: the boy's pride, the truck's suspension, and the grandfather's standing invitation to keep being the one the kid actually rides with
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the grandfather catches the word 'slow down' on his tongue and instead says 'how does the back end feel to you on this stretch?' — and lets the silence do the rest

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional manager rereading a memo she sent to twelve franchise owners announcing a new return policy that has produced six weeks of resistance
exampleSpecs.audience: a regional manager who thought a clear directive would settle the matter and is now wondering why no one is enforcing it
exampleSpecs.stakes: store-level compliance, her credibility on the next rollout, and the relationships with owners who feel they were handed an instruction instead of consulted
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she circles three sentences in the memo that began with 'Effective immediately, you will' and rewrites each as a question the owners could have answered for themselves

exampleSpecs.domain: a community-orchestra director getting the brass section to play softer in the second movement of a Dvořák piece three rehearsals before the spring concert
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer conductor working with adult amateurs who pay nothing to be there and can leave whenever they like
exampleSpecs.stakes: the balance of the performance, the goodwill of the trumpet players, and whether anyone shows up to the dress rehearsal
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the conductor stops the orchestra and asks the principal trumpet 'what do you hear from where you're sitting in measure forty-one?' rather than telling the section to back off

exampleSpecs.domain: a pediatric night-shift nurse trying to get a frightened six-year-old to swallow a bitter antibiotic at two in the morning without waking the rest of the ward
exampleSpecs.audience: a nurse who has watched the day-shift staff lose this fight three times already
exampleSpecs.stakes: the dose, the child's trust in every adult in scrubs for the rest of the stay, and the sleep of four other kids on the hall
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse considers what she would say if her only tool were a question, and lands on 'do you want it in the little cup or off the spoon, and do you want to count to three or should I?'
